description.narrative: Land degradation continues to increase at an alarming rate, with over one-third of the global land area now degraded. This degradation poses a significant threat to the well-being of 3.2 billion people and jeopardises half of the global annual GDP, which relies on natural capital. Continued land degradation will reduce our ability to meet internationally agreed-upon goals on climate, biodiversity, water and food security, including our ability to tackle current challenges of poverty and conflict, particularly in drylands. Drylands, already burdened by water scarcity, now confront the impacts of climate change in the form of more frequent droughts, increasingly severe rainfall events and warming that is twice the global average. This reality is set to accelerate current rates of degradation, to aggravate resource crises, and to increase food and nutrition insecurity. Sustainable land management and restoration serve as strategic entry points for comprehensive action, benefiting livelihoods, food security, climate resilience, and peace-making. Moreover, restoration is a cost-effective Naturebased Solution (NbS) for large-scale carbon dioxide removal and community resilience. The overall objective of this action is to accelerate sustainable land management in the world¿s drylands to achieve healthy, biodiverse landscapes, resilient livelihoods, food and water security, a safer climate, and greater peace. The Action will support global efforts to prevent, halt and reverse land degradation in drylands by (i) mobilising global action for sustainable landscapes [actions to sustainably manage and restore drylands have multiplied and are supported by more conducive policies, stronger political commitment, and sustained social movements.]; (ii) strengthening capacity, knowledge, and drive for effective action [key actors actively exchange knowledge and use proven and promising approaches, evidence, and tools to design, implement, and monitor sound restoration 1 Art. 27 NDICI Page 4 of 26 policies and actions]; and (iii) driving high-quality and large-scale action on the ground [impactful, inclusive, and sustainable management and restoration of landscapes takes place at scale in selected dryland degradation hotspots]. It will, inter alia, promote evidence-based policies and practices (notably regreening approaches such as agroforestry and farmer-managed natural regeneration, adaptive grazing management, rewilding, soil and water conservation techniques, and community-based decision-making and management), leverage and support innovative financing for restoration, and further strengthen the capacity of stakeholders for impactful action. The Action will involve collaboration with an influential set of partners to work hand-in-hand with existing global/regional initiatives such as, for example, the UN Decade on Ecosystem Restoration, 1000 Landscapes for 1 Billion People, the Global Landscapes Forum, the Bonn Challenge, the African Forest Landscape Restoration Initiative (AFR100), the Initiative 20x20 for Latin America and the Caribbean, the Landscape Partnership Asia, the UNCCD Land Degradation Neutrality, the Global Biodiversity 30x30 target, the Climate Resilient Food Systems Alliance, the Planetary Security Initiative, and the UN Food Systems Transformation Hub.
